We need:
```
Theorem noninterference : forall C t1 t2 T_secret T_result,
  has_type empty t1 T_secret -> has_type empty t2 T_secret ->
  context_has_type C T_secret T_result ->
  ground T_result -> transparent T_result ->
  ~ flows_to (security_of T_secret).(indirect_reader) (security_of T_result).(indirect_reader) ->
  same_result (plug C t1) (plug C t2).
```

This is the standard "noninterference via logical relation" where the logical relation is between two terms (binary, "indistinguishability"), and the context lemma says: if t1 ~ t2 at type T_secret (i.e., they are indistinguishable at the level of the context), then plug C t1 and plug C t2 evaluate to equal (erased) values when the result type is ground and transparent and the observer cannot read the secret's indirect level.

Given the `~ flows_to secret.indirect_reader result.indirect_reader` and `transparent T_result`, plus ground T_result.

Let's understand the `transparent` definition: `transparent T = transparent_at (security_of T) T`, where:
```

```
So `transparent T` says all nested types' security is ≤ T's security (i.e., `security_of T_i <= security_of T` for all subterms).
```coq
Fixpoint VR (o : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      ((exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\ VR o T1 u1 u2)
       \/ (exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\ VR o T2 u1 u2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ VR o T1 a1 a2 /\ VR o T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      forall (w1 w2 : tm) (r : label),
        flows_to s.(reader) r ->
        VR o T1 w1 w2 ->
        ER o (ty_protect s.(indirect_reader) T2) (tm_app v1 w1 r) (tm_app v2 w2 r)
  end
with ER (o : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> VR o T v1 v2.
```

Now, let's write out the full relation definition:

```coq
Fixpoint VR (o : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit s =>
      flows_to (indirect_reader s) o ->
      exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to (indirect_reader s) o ->
      ((exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\ VR o T1 u1 u2)
       \/ (exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\ VR o T2 u1 u2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to (indirect_reader s) o ->
      exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2,
        v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ VR o T1 a1 a2 /\ VR o T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to (indirect_reader s) o ->
      forall w1 w2 r,
        flows_to (reader s) r ->
        VR o T1 w1 w2 ->
        forall z1 z2,
          evaluates (tm_app v1 w1 r) z1 ->
          evaluates (tm_app v2 w2 r) z2 ->
          VR o T2 z1 z2
  end.

Definition ER (o : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> VR o T v1 v2.
```

Hmm, wait: in the arrow clause, should the arguments w1,w2 be related by VR (values) or ER (terms)? I earlier considered both. The decomposition lemma for app gives us t1_i ⇓ abs, t2_i ⇓ value ✓. Good.

But in the T_Abs case, the arrow clause's premise VR at T1 w1 w2 gives us the argument relation; then the body's IH needs env_rel at T1: ER at T1 of w1,w2. From VR at T1 of values w1,w2, we get ER at T1 of w1,w2 by the stability lemma (`value w → w ⇓ w` and multi from a value only reaches itself) ✓.

`subtype_interp : forall T U, subtype T U -> forall o v1 v2, VR o T v1 v2 -> VR o U v1 v2`.

- S_Unit kappa1 kappa2 Hwf1 Hwf2 Hle: T = Unit k1, U = Unit k2. VR o (Unit k1) v1 v2 = (flows_to k1.ind o → ∃ k1' k2', v1 = unit ... ∧ v2 = ...). Theorem fundamental :
```
  forall Gamma t T, has_type Gamma t T ->
  forall o g1 g2,
    env_rel o Gamma g1 g2 ->
    env_lc g1 -> env_lc g2 ->
```

```
Definition env_rel o Gamma g1 g2 :=
  forall x U, lookup_context x Gamma = Some U -> ER o U (g1 x) (g2 x).
Definition env_lc g := forall x, locally_closed (g x).
```

```
Lemma env_rel_update : forall o Gamma g1 g2 x T w1 w2,
  env_rel o Gamma g1 g2 -> ER o T w1 w2 ->
  env_rel o (update Gamma x T) (update_env g1 x w1) (update_env g2 x w2).

  destruct (Nat.eqb x y) eqn:E.

  - apply Nat.eqb_neq in E. apply Hrel.

```
Hmm, `update Gamma x T = (x,T) :: Gamma`, and `lookup y ((x,T)::Gamma) = if y =? x then Some T else lookup y Gamma`. Since x ≠ y, eqb y x = false ✓ (need Nat.eqb_neq and symmetry). Then Hlook gives lookup y Gamma = Some U ✓.

Now the commutation lemma for substitution:
```
Definition update_env (g : atom -> tm) (x : atom) (u : tm) : atom -> tm :=
  fun y => if Nat.eqb y x then u else g y.

Fixpoint subst_env (g : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm := ... (* replace fvars *)
Lemma subst_env_open : forall g x u body,
  x ∉ fv body ->
  subst_env (update_env g x u) (open body (tm_fvar x)) = open (subst_env g body) u.
```
Proof by induction on body (since open_rec recurses structurally on the term). Note `open body (tm_fvar x) = open_rec 0 (tm_fvar x) body`, and `open (subst_env g body) u = open_rec 0 u (subst_env g body)`. We need a generalized statement for open_rec at depth k:
```
forall g x u body k, x ∉ fv body ->
  subst_env (update_env g x u) (open_rec k (tm_fvar x) body) = open_rec k u (subst_env g body)
```
Induction on body; cases:
- tm_bvar i: open_rec k (fvar x) (bvar i) = if k =? i then fvar x else bvar i. subst_env (update_env g x u) of that = if k=?i then u else bvar i. RHS: open_rec k u (bvar i) = if k=?i then u else bvar i ✓.

Now, syntax: subst_env.

```coq
Fixpoint subst_env (g : atom -> tm) (t : tm) : tm :=
  match t with
  | tm_bvar i => tm_bvar i
  | tm_fvar x => g x
  | tm_unit kappa => tm_unit kappa
  | tm_abs T body kappa => tm_abs T (subst_env g body) kappa
  | tm_app t1 t2 r => tm_app (subst_env g t1) (subst_env g t2) r
  | tm_pair t1 t2 kappa => tm_pair (subst_env g t1) (subst_env g t2) kappa
  | tm_fst t1 r => tm_fst (subst_env g t1) r
  | tm_snd t1 r => tm_snd (subst_env g t1) r
  | tm_inl t1 kappa => tm_inl (subst_env g t1) kappa
  | tm_inr t1 kappa => tm_inr (subst_env g t1) kappa
  | tm_case t0 b1 b2 r => tm_case (subst_env g t0) (subst_env g b1) (subst_env g b2) r
  | tm_protect l t1 => tm_protect l (subst_env g t1)
  | tm_if c yes no r => tm_if (subst_env g c) (subst_env g yes) (subst_env g no) r
  end.
```

```coq
Definition update_env (g : atom -> tm) (x : atom) (u : tm) : atom -> tm :=
```

Let me also write the plug/subst_env lemma and fv_ctx now.

```coq
Fixpoint fv_ctx (C : program_context) : list atom :=
  match C with
  | C_Hole => []
  | C_Abs T C' kappa => fv_ctx C'
  | C_AppLeft C' t2 r => fv_ctx C' ++ fv t2
  | C_AppRight t1 C' r => fv t1 ++ fv_ctx C'
  | C_PairLeft C' t2 kappa => fv_ctx C' ++ fv t2
  | C_PairRight t1 C' kappa => fv t1 ++ fv_ctx C'
  | C_Fst C' r => fv_ctx C'
  | C_Snd C' r => fv_ctx C'
  | C_Inl C' kappa => fv_ctx C'
  | C_Inr C' kappa => fv_ctx C'
  | C_CaseScrutinee C' b1 b2 r => fv_ctx C' ++ fv b1 ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseLeft t0 C' b2 r => fv t0 ++ fv_ctx C' ++ fv b2
  | C_CaseRight t0 b1 C' r => fv t0 ++ fv b1 ++ fv_ctx C'
  | C_Protect l C' => fv_ctx C'
  | C_IfCondition C' y n r => fv_ctx C' ++ fv y ++ fv n
  | C_IfThen c C' n r => fv c ++ fv_ctx C' ++ fv n
  | C_IfElse c y C' r => fv c ++ fv y ++ fv_ctx C'
  end.
```

```coq
Fixpoint VR (o : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with

  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 s =>

  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 s =>

        v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ VR o T1 a1 a2 /\ VR o T2 b1 b2

        value w1 -> value w2 ->
```

```coq
Fixpoint VR (o : label) (T : ty) (v1 v2 : tm) : Prop :=
  match T with
  | Ty_Unit s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      exists k1 k2, v1 = tm_unit k1 /\ v2 = tm_unit k2
  | Ty_Sum T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      ((exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inl u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inl u2 k2 /\ VR o T1 u1 u2)
       \/ (exists u1 u2 k1 k2, v1 = tm_inr u1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_inr u2 k2 /\ VR o T2 u1 u2))
  | Ty_Prod T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      exists a1 b1 a2 b2 k1 k2,
        v1 = tm_pair a1 b1 k1 /\ v2 = tm_pair a2 b2 k2 /\ VR o T1 a1 a2 /\ VR o T2 b1 b2
  | Ty_Arrow T1 T2 s =>
      flows_to s.(indirect_reader) o ->
      forall (w1 w2 : tm) (r : label),
        value w1 -> value w2 ->
        flows_to s.(reader) r ->
        VR o T1 w1 w2 ->
        forall (z1 z2 : tm),
          evaluates (tm_app v1 w1 r) z1 ->
          evaluates (tm_app v2 w2 r) z2 ->
          VR o T2 z1 z2
  end.

Definition ER (o : label) (T : ty) (t1 t2 : tm) : Prop :=
  forall v1 v2, evaluates t1 v1 -> evaluates t2 v2 -> VR o T v1 v2.
```

Let me write multi_app_abs_protect:

```coq
Lemma multi_app_abs_protect : forall T body kappa v r z,
  value v -> value (tm_abs T body kappa) ->
  tm_app (tm_abs T body kappa) v r -->* z -> value z ->
  flows_to kappa.(reader) r /\

  induction Hm as [s0 | s0 s1 s2 Hs Hm IH].
  - (* multi_refl *) inversion Hz.
  - (* multi_step *) inversion Hs; subst.
    + (* ST_AppAbs *) split; assumption.
    + (* ST_App1 *) inversion H1.   (* step (abs) t1' impossible *)
    + (* ST_App2 *) exfalso; eapply value_no_step; eauto.
```

```
Lemma multi_app_abs_protect : forall s z, s -->* z -> value z ->
  forall T body kappa v r, s = tm_app (tm_abs T body kappa) v r ->
  value v -> value (tm_abs T body kappa) ->

  intros Hz T body kappa v r Heq Hv Habs.
  - subst. inversion Hz.
  - subst. inversion Hs; subst.
    + split; assumption.
```

protect_value_compose:
```
Lemma protect_value_compose : forall v l1 l2,
  protect_value (protect_value v l1) l2 = protect_value v (join l1 l2).
Proof.
  intros v l1 l2. destruct v; simpl.
  - (* bvar *) reflexivity.
  - (* fvar *) reflexivity.
  - (* unit *) rewrite protect_security_assoc. reflexivity.
  - (* abs *) rewrite protect_security_assoc. reflexivity.
  - (* app *) reflexivity.
  - (* pair *) rewrite protect_security_assoc. reflexivity.
  - (* fst *) reflexivity.
  - (* snd *) reflexivity.
  - (* inl *) rewrite protect_security_assoc. reflexivity.
  - (* inr *) rewrite protect_security_assoc. reflexivity.
  - (* case *) reflexivity.
  - (* protect *) reflexivity.
  - (* if *) reflexivity.
Qed.
```

For abs: tm_abs T body (protect_security k l1) → protect_value → tm_abs T body (protect_security (protect_security k l1) l2) ✓; RHS tm_abs T body (protect_security k (join l1 l2)) ✓ rewrite assoc.
For pair: tm_pair v1 v2 (protect k l1) → protect_value → tm_pair v1 v2 (protect (protect k l1) l2) ✓.
For inl/inr ✓.

```coq
Theorem fundamental : forall Gamma t T, has_type Gamma t T ->
  forall o g1 g2,
    env_rel o Gamma g1 g2 ->
    env_lc g1 -> env_lc g2 ->
    ER o T (subst_env g1 t) (subst_env g2 t).
```

Proof by induction on H. I'll use the `as` pattern with all argument names, as learned from has_type_ind. The branch argument lists (from the induction principle printed earlier):

- f (T_Var): Gamma x T Hlook Hwf → no IH.
- f0 (T_Unit): Gamma kappa Hwf.

- f3 (T_Pair): Gamma t1 t2 T1 T2 kappa Hty1 IH1 Hty2 IH2 Hwf.

```coq
Theorem fundamental : forall Gamma t T, has_type Gamma t T ->
  forall o (g1 g2 : atom -> tm),
    env_rel o Gamma g1 g2 -> env_lc g1 -> env_lc g2 ->
    ER o T (subst_env g1 t) (subst_env g2 t).
Proof.
  intros Gamma t T H.
  induction H as
    [ Gamma0 x T0 Hlook Hwf
    | Gamma0 kappa Hwf
    | L Gamma0 T1 body T2 kappa Hwf1 Hwf2 Hty HIH
    | Gamma0 t1 t2 T1 T2 kappa r Hty1 IH1 Hty2 IH2 Hflow
    | Gamma0 t1 t2 T1 T2 kappa Hty1 IH1 Hty2 IH2 Hwf
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa r Hty IH Hflow
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa r Hty IH Hflow
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa Hty IH HwfT2 Hwfkappa
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa HwfT1 Hty IH Hwfkappa
    | L Gamma0 t0 body1 body2 T1 T2 T0 kappa r Hty0 IH0 Hflow Hty1 IH1 Hty2 IH2
    | Gamma0 t0 T0 l Hty IH
    | Gamma0 t0 T0 U Hty IH Hsub
    | Gamma0 c yes no k T0 r Htyc IHc Htyy IHy Htyn IHn Hflow ];
  intros o g1 g2 Hrel Hlc1 Hlc2.
```

```coq
Theorem fundamental : forall Gamma t T, has_type Gamma t T ->
  forall o (g1 g2 : atom -> tm),
    env_rel o Gamma g1 g2 -> env_lc g1 -> env_lc g2 ->
    ER o T (subst_env g1 t) (subst_env g2 t).
Proof.
  intros Gamma t T H.
  induction H as
    [ Gamma0 x T0 Hlook Hwf
    | Gamma0 kappa0 Hwf
    | L Gamma0 T1 body T2 kappa0 Hwf1 Hwf2 Hty HIH
    | Gamma0 t1 t2 T1 T2 kappa0 r0 Hty1 IH1 Hty2 IH2 Hflow
    | Gamma0 t1 t2 T1 T2 kappa0 Hty1 IH1 Hty2 IH2 Hwf
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa0 r0 Hty IH Hflow
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa0 r0 Hty IH Hflow
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa0 Hty IH HwfT2 Hwfkappa
    | Gamma0 t0 T1 T2 kappa0 HwfT1 Hty IH Hwfkappa
    | L Gamma0 t0 body1 body2 T1 T2 TT kappa0 r0 Hty0 IH0 Hflow Hty1 IH1 Hty2 IH2
    | Gamma0 t0 TT l0 Hty IH
    | Gamma0 t0 TT UU Hty IH Hsub
    | Gamma0 c0 yes0 no0 k0 TT r0 Htyc IHc Htyy IHy Htyn IHn Hflow ];
  intros o g1 g2 Hrel Hlc1 Hlc2.
```

Everything up to the final theorem compiles! Now the final theorem's proof. Let me write it.

The theorem:
```
Theorem noninterference : forall (C : program_context) (t1 t2 : tm)
    (T_secret T_result : ty),
  has_type empty t1 T_secret ->
  has_type empty t2 T_secret ->
  context_has_type C T_secret T_result ->
  ground T_result ->
  transparent T_result ->
  ~ flows_to (security_of T_secret).(indirect_reader)
      (security_of T_result).(indirect_reader) ->
  same_result (plug C t1) (plug C t2).
Proof.
  intros C t1 t2 T_secret T_result Ht1 Ht2 Hctx Hg Htr Hni.
  (* choose a fresh x *)
  destruct Hctx as (L & Hctx).
  set (x := fresh (L ++ fv_ctx C ++ fv t1 ++ fv t2)).
  assert (HxL : ~ In x L) by (...).
  assert (HxC : ~ In x (fv_ctx C)) by (...).
  assert (Hx1 : ~ In x (fv t1)) by (...).
  assert (Hx2 : ~ In x (fv t2)) by (...).
  (* environments *)
  set (g1 := update_env (fun y => tm_fvar y) x t1).
  set (g2 := update_env (fun y => tm_fvar y) x t2).
  (* env_rel at update empty x T_secret *)
```
